points.text: Dataset has little novelty: pooled existing samples with open-model responses and labels
Labelling ignores compositional text-image effects on harmfulness
No category for harmful-topic inputs not seeking harmful responses
Harm categories poorly motivated, e.g., merging child and animal abuse
No inter-annotator agreement reported for human annotations
Alignment of Qwen auto-labels with human test labels not reported
Manual cleaning and annotation details missing: annotators, backgrounds, guidelines
Training set fully auto-labelled without quality control
Contribution incremental: aggregation, auto-labelling, small test set, fine-tuning
Limited novelty; no original data, scenarios or annotation methodology
Class imbalance hurts minority categories; no mitigation proposed
Only accuracy reported; no precision, recall or F1
No results across multiple random seeds
No quantitative annotation reliability metric
Data curation relies on MLLMs, capping quality at their capability
FalconEye weak on fine-grained category classification
In-domain test makes comparisons unfair; out-of-domain performance unclear
Accuracy only metric on imbalanced data; need precision/recall/F1, AUROC, confusion matrices
No inter-annotator agreement reported for Falcon-test
Annotator count, adjudication procedure and guidelines not given
Baselines not given same task/taxonomy; baseline prompts unspecified
Llama-Guard-3-Vision missing from main comparison tables
GPT-4o refusals dropped from evaluation rather than counted
No confidence intervals or seeds; small gains over GPT-4o may be noise
Train/test circularity: labels from same model family, in-distribution test; generalization unsupported
Agreement between 72B auto-labels and human labels not reported
Near-duplicate train/test leakage not addressed
Small gain over text-only Llama-Guard on BeaverTails-V weakens visual-information thesis
FalconEye below baselines in many OOD categories; 'majority' claim false
Base Qwen below chance on VLGuard suggests prompt/format failure
OOD benchmarks only partially evaluate tri-output
No comparison with other recent multimodal evaluators or guard models
No ablation of image contribution (text-only evaluator)
Category detection poor and metric undefined, contradicting claims
Responses from weak jailbroken 7B models; artificial distribution, transfer untested
Attack prompt unmentioned in main text and misreferenced
Harmful-heavy composition unrealistic; benign false-positive rate unreported
Dataset and evaluator incremental novelty
Table 1 compares only datasets; some entries unverified
Taxonomy merges and loosely defined classes; fragmentation claim untested
Numerical and naming inconsistencies across tables and text
Table 1 circularly lists FalconEye as eval method
Single training run with no validation split or model selection
Rationale quality never evaluated despite headline claim
No ethics discussion for releasing harmful content
